DIAL.name: Dialogue Topic
DIAL.note: UESP, Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/DIAL. A DIAL record defines a dialogue topic and is followed by a group holding the topic's INFO responses. [measured: 15,037 DIAL records in Skyrim.esm; SNAM is always 4 bytes, a four-character subtype code, and is not NUL-terminated]

BNAM.name: Owning Branch
BNAM.note: The dialogue branch (DLBR) that owns the topic.

DATA.name: Unknown
DATA.note: The custom and scene flags, the dialogue tab, the numeric subtype id and an unused byte. [measured: DATA is 4 bytes in all 15,037 DIAL records]

FULL.name: Player Dialogue
FULL.note: The player's dialogue, an index into the string file.

QNAM.name: Owning Quest
QNAM.note: The quest (QUST) that owns the topic.

SNAM.name: Subtype
SNAM.note: The four-character dialogue subtype, such as HELO for hello or ATCK for attack. It is not NUL-terminated, and the game uses it in preference to the numeric subtype id in DATA.

TIFC.name: Info Count
TIFC.note: How many INFO records the topic has. The game uses it to preallocate the topic's info list, but it is not required.

INFO.name: Dialogue Topic Info
INFO.note: UESP, Skyrim Mod:Mod File Format/INFO. An INFO record is one response to a dialogue topic. DATA and ENAM are exclusive: DATA is seen on record versions 31 and lower and ENAM on versions 31 and higher, though version 31 itself may carry either but not both. The response's text and notes are a group of NAM1, NAM2 and NAM3. [measured: 31,465 INFO records in Skyrim.esm; TRDT is always 24 bytes]

CNAM.name: Favor Level
CNAM.note: The favor the response requires: 0 = None, 3 = Large.

CTDA.name: Conditions
CTDA.note: The conditions that must be true for this dialogue to be available.

DATA.name: Dialogue Tab And Flags
DATA.note: The dialogue tab, the response's flags and the reset time in days. Only on record versions 31 and lower.

DNAM.name: Shared Info
DNAM.note: The info whose response data to show instead. When a record has both, the shared info appears to override the responses.

ENAM.name: Flags And Reset Time
ENAM.note: The response's flags and the reset time in hours, where 0 is 0 hours and 0xFFFF is 24. Only on record versions 31 and higher.

struct.name: flags
struct.note: The response's flags. Bit 11 is inverted from the CK's display.

struct.name: reset_time
struct.note: Hours until the response resets. Scaled, so 0 is 0 hours and 0xFFFF is 24.

NAM1.name: Response Text
NAM1.note: The dialogue string shown in the game, an index into the string file.

NAM2.name: Response Notes
NAM2.note: The actor's notes. The game does not load it.

NAM3.name: Response Edits
NAM3.note: The response's edits. The game does not load it.

NEXT.name: Marker
NEXT.note: Zero-length; it separates the SCHR fields.

PNAM.name: Previous Info
PNAM.note: The previous topic info. Never present in Skyrim.esm, and always present in the other files.

SCHR.name: Old Script
SCHR.note: The old scripting info. When it is present at all the fields always include an SCHR grouping, a NEXT, and another SCHR grouping.

TCLT.name: Topic Links
TCLT.note: The follow-up topics after this one.

TRDT.name: Response
TRDT.note: The response's emotion, sound and number.
